paper.title_en: $B\to K a$ decays in QCD factorization and revised bounds on ALP couplings
paper.abstract_en: Rare flavor-changing processes such as $B\to K a$ offer sensitive probes of axion-like particles (ALPs) for masses below a few GeV. We study this process in the framework of QCD factorization and ALP effective theory, in which the ALP couples to the Standard Model (SM) fermions through shift-invariant derivative interactions. In contrast to previous studies, where flavor violation arises solely from flavor-changing ALP couplings, we also include the contributions proportional to flavor-conserving ALP couplings, in which the flavor change is mediated by the weak interactions of the SM. Based on this analysis, we derive upper bounds on both flavor-changing and flavor-conserving ALP couplings at low energies. Then we consider the UV scenario of a "minimally flavor-violating ALP", which features flavor-universal ALP-fermion couplings at very high energies, and evaluate the resulting constraints on the UV couplings.
